record.interface_detail: Standard frpc against a published node, privilege port and password.
record.chaining: A 1 TB one-way free frp node that can carry a WG UDP tunnel, if the 2019-era node is still up.
record.binding_note: if the operator means TiB it passes. There is no other cap in the way.

identity_cost.detail: The page publishes the privilege port and password per node; no account is required to use a node.

record.reliability_note: Weekly restart at 03:00 Monday; node IPs were blocked at national level twice in 2019.
record.confidence_note: The node table is on the page today. A clarification of TB versus TiB, or a measured month, would move the verdict.

evidence.proved: US Buffalo node: 1000M shared, 1T one-way traffic, 5 mappings, ports 20000-50000, public privilege password
Dallas and Russia nodes also list 1T one-way traffic at 100M shared

record.notes: The closest free frp endpoint to the volume bar, and anonymous. Its history section is the useful part: a 2019 note says a user running a proxy got 222.222.0.0/8 blocked wholesale, which is the blast radius of a shared free endpoint. Node pages date from 2019 and the server version is 0.60.0, so uptime today is unproven.

extras.wg_detail: The page introduces frp as supporting tcp, udp, http and https and gives a privilege port, an xtcp port and a monitor port per node; a WG datagram can be proxied on a port in 20000-50000.
extras.volume_stated: Server traffic 1T, one-way, per the node table. Whether that is a decimal TB or a TiB is not stated.
